newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA JAN-APRIL BUDGET GAP AT 2.43 TRLN LEI.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA JAN-APRIL BUDGET GAP AT 2.43 TRLN LEI.

text.p: Romania's state budget deficit widened to 2.43 trillion lei ($338 million) over January-April from 1.98 trillion in the first quarter of this year, central bank data (BNR) showed on Tuesday.

State revenues climbed by 3.39 trillion lei in April to 9.96 trillion lei in the first four months of 1997. Spending was 12.4 trillion lei at end-April, sharply up from 8.45 trillion over January-March, BNR data showed.
Last month, Finance Minister Mircea Ciumara said the 1997 budget would be revised in July to include recent moves in macro-economic indicators, as well as new fiscal rules.
Under the current 1997 budget -- agreed with international lenders -- the state budget gap was set at 12.6 trillion lei, or 5.4 percent, of gross domestic product.
It also put year-on-year inflation at 90 percent, but the impact of price liberalisation was higher than expected, with consumer prices 96.7 percent up in May from December 1996.
Romanian officials have recently revised inflation estimates upward, putting the year-on-year figure at 110 to 120 percent. That figure is likely to be included in the revised budget.
The revised budget is also expected to include government pledges to ease income and profit taxes -- now at up to 60 percent and 38 percent respectively -- in the second half of this year.

The deficit under the consolidated budget -- including state budget, local government budgets, social security budget, supplementary pension funds and various other extra-budgetary funds -- is to be trimmed to 4.5 percent of the GDP from 5.8 percent in 1996.
